thread:
emma: Heads up, ran into a weird cancellation -> retry race with the Android SDK + Retrofit on a production-ish sample. When a coroutine is cancelled (timeout) the underlying OkHttp call sometimes completes and triggers our retrofit retry wrapper, resulting in duplicate requests and double token-refresh.

ryan: Oof. Which retry path are you using in the SDK? Our wrapper or OkHttp's internal retry?

emma: SDK wrapper (suspend adapter around Retrofit's Call). We also add a lightweight retry for idempotent endpoints. But the sequence is: coroutine times out -> caller cancels -> but Call.execute still returns on a different thread -> wrapper sees exception vs success inconsistently and retries.

dani: Can you paste the minimal repro? Even a pseudocode snippet helps.

emma: Sure, gist of the flow: ```kotlin
suspend fun gen(req: Req): Resp = withTimeout(5_000) {
  try { api.generate(req) }
  catch(e: IOException) { retry(...) }
}
// Retrofit return is a suspend fn that under the hood calls Call.await()
```

emma: On a flaky network the coroutine times out, but OkHttp's network thread finishes the response a few ms later. The SDK retry wrapper doesn't see the cancellation consistently because the exception type varies (CancellationException vs IOException) depending on where the timing hits.

leo: Are you using Call.cancel() in a CoroutineCancellation handler? Retrofit's suspend adapter should cancel the Call for you but some adapter versions had a bug. Which versions?

emma: Retrofit 2.9.0, OkHttp 4.10.0, kotlin coroutines 1.6.4. We also hit this on devices >= Android 8.

ryan: I remember a bug where OkHttp's CallCancellation on coroutine cancel could race if the call already completed but callback hasn't posted back. The fix was to ensure the retry wrapper checks coroutineContext.isActive before performing a retry and to prefer throwing CancellationException upstream.

dani: Temporary mitigations: 1) in your retry wrapper add a pre-retry check: if (!isActive) throw CancellationException("coroutine cancelled") ; 2) make token refresh idempotent (use in-flight request locking) so duplicate refreshes are harmless.

emma: Implemented #1 and it stopped the duplicate retries in the emulator. Token refresh still had a tiny window where two refreshes fire; added an in-process mutex and that fixed it.

leo: We should add a small change to the SDK: a utility function for suspend retries that respects coroutine cancellation and also exposes a parameter to make retries skip on CancellationException. That would avoid smart callers from accidentally re-trying cancelled work.

ryan: Also file an issue to test this scenario in CI using robolectric/emulator network drop to ensure no regressions. Owner? @dani?

dani: I'll own the test. Plan: add a vm-run of the sampleapp in CI that toggles the emulator network and asserts no duplicate token-refresh calls recorded.

emma: Creating GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-android/issues/499 (draft) with logs + minimal repro.

devx-bot: New issue created: sdk-android#499 — "android: coroutine cancellation race causes duplicate retries and token-refresh" (assigned to @emma).

ryan: Action items: 1) SDK change: add cancellation-aware retry helper (owner: leo), 2) Test: emulator network toggle E2E (owner: dani), 3) Docs: onboarding note about using SDK suspend helpers and cancellation semantics (owner: emma).

emma: Will add a short blurb to the mobile onboarding doc and link the issue. Thanks! :pray:
